placements.title: organizational memory shifts from accumulation to deliberate forgetting
placements.frame: What specific knowledge is being ordered forgotten or removed, and what does the choice of target reveal about what the organization no longer wants carried forward?
placements.why: Both segments carry the same content theme despite naming unrelated targets (a named decision vs. a named migration): an instruction to actively discard specific accumulated knowledge from the organization's memory. This is a subject future envelopes could keep feeding — more directives to forget or remove particular items — rather than a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test (a statement true beyond the words describing this one instance: 'knowledge here gets deliberately erased, not just added to'). The targets themselves ('the Quantum Widget Decision', 'the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration') were separately bound as new/unattested referents by pass-2 and are not themselves leaves — per rule 2, a leaf is the thematic container ('directives to erase knowledge'), not the erased fact or artifact. No existing structure was available to reuse: both EXISTING STRATA and EXISTING GRAPH STRUCTURE are empty for this repo, and the only loaded focus nodes (Knowledge Gap Mapping decision, Xena Githubber actor) are unrelated in subject — they describe knowledge diagnostics/mapping, not erasure. Nothing existing is even close enough to warrant a lineage edge, so this mints standalone with no forced parent; a strata-tier mint was not warranted since the content is leaf-grain (a specific directive pattern), not an organizational category the way Architecture or Product are.
